headline: Cyber alert: Bangladesh Bank restores website after 2.5-day shutdown
summary: Several banks and government agencies took their websites offline as a precaution following a critical security flaw in PHP, a widely used web programming language.
details: Bangladesh Bank restored its website after keeping it offline for two and a half days due to a critical cyber security alert. Other institutions, including Agrani, Janata, and Bengal Commercial banks, also experienced service disruptions.

The shutdowns were a precautionary measure following a security flaw in PHP, one of the world's most common web programming languages. The flaw, known as 'PHP2Shell', could allow hackers to remotely run malicious code and access sensitive data like passwords and API keys.
The land ministry also suspended its digital land services (land.gov.bd) for 36 hours following an urgent alert from BGD e-GOV CIRT, the government's cyber security agency.

Security researchers at Wiz estimate that this vulnerability could affect approximately 70 percent of websites globally. Similar precautions were taken worldwide, with 32 government services taken offline in the UK, and sites also shut down in France, Denmark, and Finland.

Experts estimate that 60 to 85 percent of websites in Bangladesh could be vulnerable. Some older systems may face challenges during updates, as it is uncertain if they will remain functional after patching.
To mitigate risks, authorities are advised to update PHP versions, use firewalls as temporary safeguards, and review server logs for any signs of unauthorized access.
caption:
A critical flaw in a global programming language forced Bangladesh Bank and other agencies to pull their websites offline to prevent hacking.

Bangladesh Bank restored its website after keeping it offline for two and a half days due to a critical cyber security alert. Other institutions, including Agrani, Janata, and Bengal Commercial banks, also experienced service disruptions.

The shutdowns were a precautionary measure following a security flaw in PHP, one of the world's most common web programming languages. The flaw, known as 'PHP2Shell', could allow hackers to remotely run malicious code and access sensitive data like passwords and API keys.

The land ministry also suspended its digital land services (land.gov.bd) for 36 hours following an urgent alert from BGD e-GOV CIRT, the government's cyber security agency.

Security researchers at Wiz estimate that this vulnerability could affect approximately 70 percent of websites globally. Similar precautions were taken worldwide, with 32 government services taken offline in the UK, and sites also shut down in France, Denmark, and Finland.

Experts estimate that 60 to 85 percent of websites in Bangladesh could be vulnerable. Some older systems may face challenges during updates, as it is uncertain if they will remain functional after patching.

To mitigate risks, authorities are advised to update PHP versions, use firewalls as temporary safeguards, and review server logs for any signs of unauthorized access.

headline_marked: [[HSC and equivalent exam results]] to be published on October 29
headline: HSC and equivalent exam results to be published on October 29
summary: The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee has announced the publication date for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate and equivalent examinations. Further details regarding the results will be released on October 26.
details: The results of this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are scheduled for publication on October 29.
The decision was finalized on Saturday following a meeting at the Ministry of Education, attended by the Education Minister and the Secretary.
Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chairman of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee and also the chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka, confirmed the date.
He also stated that more specific information concerning the results will be announced on October 26, providing students and guardians with advance notice.
